title: Functorial flasque augmented tensor complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\varphi:F\to F_1$ and $\psi:G\to G_1$ be morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. There exist integer-indexed cochain complexes $K,L,M,K_1,L_1,M_1$, zero in negative degrees and with flasque terms, and quasi-isomorphic augmentations $a,b,c,a_1,b_1,c_1$ from $F[0],G[0],(F\otimes G)[0],F_1[0],G_1[0],(F_1\otimes G_1)[0]$, respectively. There exist tensor cochain maps $u:\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes L)\to M$ and $u_1:\operatorname{Tot}(K_1\otimes L_1)\to M_1$ whose degree-zero section formulas are ordinary tensor sections followed by the target augmentation. There exist cochain maps $l:K\to K_1$, $r:L\to L_1$, $t:M\to M_1$ commuting with these augmentations over $\varphi,\psi,\varphi\otimes\psi$, and $t\circ u=u_1\circ\operatorname{tensorHom}(l,r)$. The stalk-product models are those of [def-sc-module-cup-godement-model]. No injective comparison or cohomology class equation is asserted. The tensor monoidal structure is additive (the conventional MonoidalPreadditive instance supplied for scheme modules by SheafOfModules.tensorClosed).

source.place: Lemma 20.30.1 (Tag 0FKS), functorial Godement resolution; Tag 0FKU, naive cup product and flasque construction of Lemma 20.31.4 (0FKV); natural Alexander--Whitney formula

proof.text: Construct the six concrete Godement cosimplicial models. In degree n apply the (n+1)-fold stalk-product functor to phi, psi and phi tensor psi. Naturality of the germ unit and stalk evaluation makes these maps commute with the specified cofaces and codegeneracies and with the degree-zero augmentations. Take alternating coface complexes and extend by zero to integer degrees. This functorial action is the extra construction not supplied by the existential one-pair model statements.

The augmented Godement stalk contraction proves all six augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Each nonnegative term is a product-of-stalks sheaf and is flasque; each negative term is zero. The six complexes are strictly nonnegative, and all their terms are flasque.

Use coordinatewise stalk tensor pairings on the two triples of models. Their naturality in both coefficients gives a commuting square with the three cosimplicial coefficient maps. Apply the front/back Alexander--Whitney formula to the pairings. The formula commutes with coefficient maps because all its face maps do, giving u composed with t equals tensorHom(l,r) composed with u1. The zero-degree components agree with tensoring the augmentation sections, yielding both displayed formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_godement_coefficient_complexes (X : Scheme.{v})
    [MonoidalPreadditive X.Modules] (F G F₁ G₁ : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ F₁) (ψ : G ⟶ G₁) :
    ∃ (K L M : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
      (a : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F ⟶ K)
      (b : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G ⟶ L)
      (c : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (F ⊗ G) ⟶ M),
      QuasiIso a ∧ QuasiIso b ∧ QuasiIso c ∧
      K.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ L.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ M.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (K.X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (L.X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (M.X n))) ∧
      ∃ u : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj K L ⟶ M,
        (∀ (V : X.Opens)
          (x : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F).X 0, V))
          (y : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G).X 0, V)),
          (u.f 0).val.app (op V)
            ((HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L 0 0 0 (by simp)).val.app (op V)
              (tmulSection ((a.f 0).val.app (op V) x) ((b.f 0).val.app (op V) y))) =
            (c.f 0).val.app (op V) (tmulSection x y)) ∧
    ∃ (K₁ L₁ M₁ : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
      (a₁ : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F₁ ⟶ K₁)
      (b₁ : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G₁ ⟶ L₁)
      (c₁ : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (F₁ ⊗ G₁) ⟶ M₁),
      QuasiIso a₁ ∧ QuasiIso b₁ ∧ QuasiIso c₁ ∧
      K₁.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ L₁.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ M₁.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (K₁.X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (L₁.X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (M₁.X n))) ∧
      ∃ u₁ : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj K₁ L₁ ⟶ M₁,
        (∀ (V : X.Opens)
          (x : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F₁).X 0, V))
          (y : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G₁).X 0, V)),
          (u₁.f 0).val.app (op V)
            ((HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K₁ L₁ 0 0 0 (by simp)).val.app (op V)
              (tmulSection ((a₁.f 0).val.app (op V) x) ((b₁.f 0).val.app (op V) y))) =
            (c₁.f 0).val.app (op V) (tmulSection x y)) ∧
        ∃ (l : K ⟶ K₁) (r : L ⟶ L₁) (t : M ⟶ M₁),
          a ≫ l = (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ ≫ a₁ ∧
          b ≫ r = (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map ψ ≫ b₁ ∧
          c ≫ t = (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map
            (@id (F ⊗ G ⟶ F₁ ⊗ G₁) (φ ⊗ₘ ψ)) ≫ c₁ ∧
          u ≫ t = HomologicalComplex.tensorHom l r ≫ u₁
